key_insight: DFT-derived stacking-fault energy surfaces enable reliable PFDD predictions of widening stacking faults with increasing Al content, while surfaces from both tested interatomic potentials cause premature partial-dislocation pinning.
engineering_relevance: Accurate alloy deformation modelling requires interatomic potentials that reproduce the shear-energy landscape, not just lattice parameters and elastic moduli.
method: Generate Cu–Al generalized stacking-fault energy surfaces using DFT, embedded-atom ZW and machine-learned GAP potentials.
Incorporate each energy surface into phase field dislocation dynamics (PFDD) simulations to predict equilibrium stacking-fault widths.
Compare energy landscapes and predicted widths with standalone MD results and available experimental values.
evidence_signal: Despite reasonable agreement in lattice parameters and elastic moduli, both potential-derived surfaces differ substantially from DFT at seven characteristic points; DFT-based widths agree well with standalone MD measurements and experimental values for pure Cu.
watch_item: Experimental width agreement is reported for pure Cu; validation across alloy compositions remains important before broader engineering use.
paper_title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
